chief_complaint: new severe temple headache, jaw pain when chewing, and transient vision darkening
hpi_details: 73M presenting with right temporal headache, jaw claudication, scalp tenderness, amaurosis fugax, and ESR 98 mm/hr requiring immediate high-dose prednisone before biopsy.
ideas: He thinks his temple headache and jaw ache are being caused by a severe tooth abscess or a pinched nerve in his neck.
concerns: He is terrified that the sudden darkening in his vision means he is having mini-strokes and is about to go permanently blind.
expectations: He hopes to get an urgent brain scan and immediate treatment to protect his vision before leaving the clinic today.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Giant Cell Arteritis with Polymyalgia Rheumatica evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Giant Cell Arteritis with Polymyalgia Rheumatica is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Giant Cell Arteritis with Polymyalgia Rheumatica, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: new severe temple headache, jaw pain when chewing, and transient vision darkening
Key HPI features: 73M presenting with right temporal headache, jaw claudication, scalp tenderness, amaurosis fugax, and ESR 98 mm/hr requiring immediate high-dose prednisone before biopsy.
Objective/Exam findings: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Giant Cell Arteritis with Polymyalgia Rheumatica.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Giant Cell Arteritis with Polymyalgia Rheumatica.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Trigeminal neuralgia without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Any vision changes (amaurosis fugax) — treat immediately with steroids to prevent permanent blindness.
management_principles: Visual symptoms or suspected ischemia require same-day emergency assessment by ophthalmology/rheumatology; the treating clinician should begin urgent glucocorticoid treatment without waiting for confirmatory testing when GCA is strongly suspected.
Arrange temporal-artery ultrasound and/or biopsy promptly, plus ESR/CRP, CBC, metabolic profile, and assessment for aortic involvement; testing should not delay emergency care for threatened vision.
Monitor glucocorticoid adverse effects (glucose, blood pressure, bone protection, infection risk) and use steroid-sparing therapy only under specialist direction.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with symptoms of Giant Cell Arteritis with Polymyalgia Rheumatica: new severe temple headache, jaw pain when chewing, and transient vision darkening. 73M presenting with right temporal headache, jaw claudication, scalp tenderness, amaurosis fugax, and ESR 98 mm/hr requiring immediate high-dose prednisone before biopsy.
reference_soap.objective: Document visual acuity and fields, pupils, full neurologic examination, temporal-artery tenderness/pulse, scalp tenderness, jaw claudication, and vital signs. ESR is 98 mm/hr; obtain CRP, CBC/platelets, metabolic profile, and urgent vascular/temporal-artery imaging or biopsy as locally available.
reference_soap.assessment: High suspicion for giant cell arteritis with transient visual ischemia; this is an ophthalmologic emergency with risk of permanent blindness.
reference_soap.plan: 1. Send immediately for emergency ophthalmology/rheumatology evaluation. 2. A treating clinician should start urgent glucocorticoid therapy when suspicion is high; do not wait for biopsy or ultrasound if vision is threatened. 3. Confirm diagnosis promptly and monitor treatment toxicity, blood pressure, glucose, bone protection, and infection risk.

teaching.diagnosis: Giant Cell Arteritis with Polymyalgia Rheumatica
teaching.one_liner: Inflammation of medium and large arteries — most dangerously the temporal artery — causing headache, jaw pain when chewing, and transient vision loss; an ophthalmologic emergency treated with high-dose steroids before biopsy confirmation.
red_flags: Any vision changes (amaurosis fugax) — treat immediately with steroids to prevent permanent blindness

must_ask.say: Where exactly is the headache, and is it new for you?
Does your jaw hurt or get tired when you chew?
Have you had any episodes of vision going dark or blurry?
Is your scalp tender to touch, like when you brush your hair?
Have you had stiffness or aching in your shoulders and hips?

history.answer: Doctor, I've had this terrible pain in my right temple for the past few days, and my vision went dark for a moment earlier today.
It started gradually about five days ago as a dull ache, but over the last two days it has become constant and intensely severe.
The pain is present all day long now without letting up. I have never had a headache like this before in my entire life.
It is mainly located in my right temple and above my right ear. It also feels like it spreads across the right side of my scalp.
It feels like a deep, throbbing ache that never stops. I would rate the severity at about an eight out of ten.
The headache stays with me all day, but it feels especially bad when I wake up first thing in the morning.
Touching my temple or brushing my hair makes it hurt much worse. Resting quietly helps slightly, but nothing really takes it away.
About three hours ago, a dark shade suddenly fell over my right eye for about five minutes before clearing up completely. It terrified me.
No, I didn't see any flashing lights, jagged lines, or spots before my vision darkened.
Yes, whenever I chew food like meat or bread, my jaw cramps up and aches so badly that I have to stop eating.
Yes, brushing my hair on the right side hurts so much that I can barely touch the brush to my scalp.
For the past month, my shoulders and hips have been dreadfully stiff and sore every morning, making it hard to get out of bed.
I felt slightly nauseous because the pain was so intense, but I haven't thrown up. Bright lights do bother my eyes a little right now.
No, my right eye isn't bloodshot, and it hasn't been watering or tearing up.
I haven't checked with a thermometer, but I've felt slightly feverish and fatigued over the past week with a poor appetite.
No, my neck moves freely without stiffness, and I haven't noticed any rashes on my skin.
No, I haven't had any weakness in my arms or legs, no numbness, and my speech has been completely normal.
No, I haven't bumped my head or had any falls recently.
I tried taking extra-strength Tylenol and ibuprofen yesterday, but neither helped the pain at all.
I can't think of any trigger like stress or certain foods. It just started on its own and kept getting worse.
No, no one else at home has a headache, and our heating system was serviced recently without any issues.
No, I have never had cancer, and I don't take any medications that weaken my immune system.
I thought I might have an infected tooth or a pinched nerve in my jaw and neck that is shooting pain up into my temple.
My eyesight went completely black for a moment, and I'm terrified that I'm about to have a major stroke or go blind.
I have high blood pressure and slightly elevated cholesterol, both diagnosed about ten years ago.
I had an appendectomy when I was a teenager, but I have never been hospitalized as an adult.
I take lisinopril 10 milligrams once every morning for my blood pressure.
I do not have any allergies to medications that I know of.
I have never smoked cigarettes in my life.
I only have an occasional glass of red wine with dinner on weekends.
I work full-time as an accountant, and I live at home with my wife.
My father had high blood pressure, but there is no family history of aneurysms, early strokes, or autoimmune conditions.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 138/84 mmHg, heart rate 76 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, temperature 37.1 degrees Celsius, oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Elderly male sitting upright, appearing uncomfortable and wincing while gently touching his right temple.
Visual acuity 20/25 in right eye and 20/20 in left eye; visual fields full to confrontation, pupils equal and reactive without afferent pupillary defect, funduscopy shows sharp optic disc margins.
Right temporal artery is prominent, thickened, and tender to palpation with diminished pulse; marked right scalp tenderness elicited by gentle touch.
No tenderness upon palpation or percussion over the frontal and maxillary sinuses bilaterally.
Neck is supple with full passive flexion; Kernig and Brudzinski signs are absent.
Cranial nerves II through XII intact, extraocular movements full without nystagmus, facial sensation and motor symmetry preserved.
Full 5/5 muscle strength throughout upper and lower extremities, though active shoulder and hip abduction is mildly limited by proximal muscle stiffness.
Sensation to light touch and pinprick is symmetrically preserved across all dermatomes.
Normal finger-to-nose and rapid alternating movements; steady gait without ataxia.
Bilateral shoulder and hip girdles show reduced active range of motion due to stiffness, without joint effusion, erythema, or warmth.
